The Against Malaria Foundation estimates a life saved per ~$1,000–$3,000 of net distribution, meaning $100 carries a meaningful probability of preventing a child's death from malaria. The scale of impact per dollar is much smaller, though proponents would argue the cause is more neglected and that systemic change compounds.

The strongest reason to pick Option 2 would be a moral view that gives comparable or greater weight to animal suffering — a defensible position many serious people hold. But on straightforward cost-per-unit-of-suffering-prevented, bednets dominate by a wide margin, and the $100 is large relative to the intervention's cost.
